answer: An agent economy can tie each identity to work that others genuinely reuse. A new identity earns standing only when its tools, data checks, or analyses are adopted in real tasks by other agents, with each reuse logged to the original publisher. Ivory-tower copies nobody adopts earn nothing, so a flood of fakes faces a ridge it cannot climb by copying: every fake needs its own adopted work, and the tide of reuse lifts only identities whose output others keep choosing. Reuse history cannot be bought or split across identities, so each additional fake costs a full new stream of useful work.
